testId: testim-migrated/tests/webstore/quick-order/verification-of-paste-multiple-section-for-guest-user.spec.ts > Webstore - Quick Order > verification of paste multiple section for guest user

scenario.summary: Guest uses Quick Order: pastes two SKUs with quantities (Paste Multiple) and gets the 2-products toast; enters the same SKU in two rows and gets the duplicate error; submits five SKU rows (simple and bundle products) to the cart; a product with a required add-on is rejected; a quantity above the product maximum is rejected.
steps: Guest session (empty storageState); open Quick Order > Add Multiple Items > Paste Multiple.
Paste '<sku>, 10\n<variant sku>, 5' and add; toast '2 Products were added to your 'Quick List'.'; clear the cart.

Multiple rows: type the duplicate product SKU in row 0 and row 1 (suggestion '<name> | <sku>' each time); 'The product already exists.'; Add to Cart; cart heading 'Cart' and the cart line shows the product name; clear the cart.
Multiple rows 0-4: four simple products and one bundle product, each checked by its suggestion text; Add to Cart; 'Cart'; clear the cart.
Row 0: product with a required add-on; suggestion text; the mandatory personalization/add-on error is shown; clear row 0.
Row 0: product with a maximum quantity; suggestion text; set quantity to maximum + 1 (101 recorded); the quantity range error is shown.
stateChanges: Guest session cart receives the pasted products, the duplicate-check product and the five row products; it is cleared after each step (no order placed).
assertions: Paste Multiple toast contains '2 Products were added to your 'Quick List'.'
Duplicate SKU error 'The product already exists.' is visible
Cart heading equals 'Cart'; the cart line contains the duplicate-check product name
Required add-on product: 'This product requires a mandatory personalized message/add-ons and, therefore, can not be added to the list.' is visible
Quantity above the maximum: 'Selected quantity should be in between 1 to 100' (min to max of the product) is visible
evidence: Title 'verification of paste multiple section for guest user' and step labels 1) to 5) match the flow; no linked cases, no AIO file.
Store MaxwellsHardware: the webstore every migrated webstore spec runs on (testimEnv.web.baseUrl, webstore-z10-at); same store as the approved pdp/plp/my-account entries.

Suggestion texts are recorded as '<name> | <sku>' (e.g. 'American Standard Gold 95v Furnace | z-1234570'): role data of the product need; the migrated spec builds `${p.name} | ${p.sku}` from the need outputs (name, sku). Names can themselves contain ' | ' (z-1234575 'Daikin FHQ-CB | Multi-Split Air Conditioning Unit').

pasteMultipleProductList 'z-2430004, 10\nz-2510001, 5' is built from needs: line 1 = pastedProduct.sku with quantity 10, line 2 = pastedVariant.variant1Sku with quantity 5 (quantities are config, kept in the spec or data). The success message '2 Products were added to your 'Quick List'.' is expected-output: fixed UI text whose count equals the number of pasted lines (2).

z-2430004 (paste line 1, qty 10): tda rows SimpleProduct, DontTrackInventory, Min 1 / Max 100; in this test it is not a separate source (only inside the paste list), so pastedProduct = PRODUCT_SIMPLE_IN_STOCK {quantityUsed 10, minMaxQuantity 10, store} has no preferred.

z-2510001 (PimProductId 532, SimpleProduct, DontTrackInventory, Min 1 / Max 100, tda rows) is the default variant of configurable B-100004 (approved checkout / saved-cart entries). Need pastedVariant = PRODUCT_CONFIGURABLE_WITH_VARIANTS {quantityUsed 5, minVariants 1, minAddOns 0, minPersonalizableAttributes 0, variantAttributes BulbSize,Color,Technology (the value the approved entries use for B-100004; the test picks no attributes, the param is required)} -> output variant1Sku. No preferred: the recorded variant SKU only appears inside the paste-list string, not as its own source. REVIEW: the key does not check that the variant itself allows quantity 5 (MaximumQuantity) or that quick order accepts a variant SKU; the recording shows it does for z-2510001.

sku1 z-2460005: profile FOUND active SimpleProduct, inventory 250, storefront index 1, requiredAddOnCount 0 (tda rows: Min 1 / Max 100). Need duplicateProduct = PRODUCT_SIMPLE_IN_STOCK {quantityUsed 1, store}, preferred sku1: typed in rows 0 and 1, the second is rejected ('The product already exists.'), one unit goes to the cart. bosch120voltText -> '<name> | <sku>', bosch120voltText2 (cart line) -> duplicateProduct.name.

Five rows (sku2..sku6, default quantity 1): rowProduct1..3 and rowProduct4 = PRODUCT_SIMPLE_IN_STOCK {quantityUsed 1, store}, preferred sku2, sku3, sku4, sku6 (profile FOUND active simple, inventory 453, 4998, 235, 999931, requiredAddOnCount 0); skuN -> alias.sku, skuNName -> '<name> | <sku>'.

sku5 z-858585: profile FOUND active BundleProduct, storefront index 1, requiredAddOnCount 0 (no own inventory row; bundle stock is the children). Need bundleProduct = PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IN_STOCK {quantityUsed 1, minAddOns 0, minPersonalizableAttributes 0, store}, preferred sku5. sku5 -> bundleProduct.sku, sku5Name -> '<name> | <sku>'.

Recorded row products z-1234570, z-2420004, z-1234567 (and z-2470006, z-2410001) have storefront index 0 in the profile, so they do not qualify as preferred for keys that require index >= 1; the resolver falls back to an indexed product (stricter than the recording: the quick-order autocomplete found them anyway). REVIEW: the suggestion assertion reads the first suggestion; a resolved SKU that is a prefix of other SKUs could show another product first.

sku7 z-2470006: profile FOUND active SimpleProduct, inventory 250, requiredAddOnCount 1 (tda rows: ZnodePimAddOnProduct PimAddOnProductId 4, group 3, RequiredType Required), storefront index 0. Quick order rejects it with 'This product requires a mandatory personalized message/add-ons ...'. Need requiredAddOnProduct = PRODUCT_SIMPLE_WITH_REQUIRED_ADDON {quantityUsed 1, minRequiredAddOns 1, store} (personalizationAttribute left out: the message covers add-ons too). Preferred sku7 (falls back: the key needs storefront index >= 1, recorded index 0). sku7 -> requiredAddOnProduct.sku, sku7Name -> '<name> | <sku>'. The message is expected-output (fixed UI text).

sku8 z-2410001: profile FOUND active SimpleProduct, inventory 250, storefront index 0; tda rows: OutOfStockOptions DontTrackInventory, MinimumQuantity 1, MaximumQuantity 100. The test sets quantity 101 (spec literal) and expects 'Selected quantity should be in between 1 to 100': the 100 is the product's MaximumQuantity, 101 = MaximumQuantity + 1. Need maxQuantityProduct = PRODUCT_SIMPLE_IN_STOCK {quantityUsed 1, store, minMaxQuantity 1 (a numeric MaximumQuantity exists), outOfStockOption DontTrackInventory (as recorded, so the stock check cannot pre-empt the range message)}; the migrated spec types maxQuantityProduct.maxQuantity + 1 and builds the message from maxQuantity. Preferred sku8 (falls back: storefront index 0). No new key needed for 'max quantity 100': the existing output maxQuantity carries it.

MISSING OUTPUT PRODUCT_SIMPLE_IN_STOCK.minQuantity: the message lower bound '1' is the product's MinimumQuantity attribute (required PIM attribute 22, value 1 on the recorded product); the key returns maxQuantity but not minQuantity. Proposal: add output minQuantity (MinimumQuantity attribute value, same OUTER APPLY as maxQuantity with code MinimumQuantity), so quantityExceedingMessage is built as 'Selected quantity should be in between {minQuantity} to {maxQuantity}'. Until then the spec would keep the literal 1 (fallback products may differ).

Distinct records: every product alias is a separate need; the PRODUCT_SIMPLE_IN_STOCK aliases resolve to different SKUs (identity sku), which the steps need anyway (duplicate-check product must differ from the five-row products, which must differ from each other).
Literal 101 (setQuantity, spec code) is not a scanned value; it becomes maxQuantityProduct.maxQuantity + 1 in the migrated spec.

migrate: suggestion texts and the paste list combine several outputs ('<name> | <sku>', '<sku>, <qty>\n<sku>, <qty>'), so they map to no single output; the quantity-exceeding message and the spec literal 101 depend on the product's MaximumQuantity; the spec imports the JSON directly (import rawData ... then loadData). Swap rules 2 and 3 fail.
